result.title: Automated Detection and Encoding of Cartographic Signs in Historical Maps
result.summary: Symbols and icons in archival maps represent an expansive source of evidence for historical geography. In this paper, we present a two-stage framework for (1) detecting cartographic signs in historical maps and (2) generating interpretable sign embeddings that capture both semantics and stylistic variations. We also introduce CaSiDD, an open benchmark dataset spanning multiple sign categories and diverse cartographic styles, designed for generic sign detection. Using YOLOv10-X, we demonstrate the practicality of automated sign detection on historical maps. We then present strategies for creating contrasted, informative embeddings of cartographic signs. We approach embedding design systematically, maximizing expressiveness while suppressing digitization or background material confounders. Our final method, based on an adapted RADIOv4 backbone, effectively encodes both sign form and semantics, while producing interpretable representations. This work lays a foundation for scalable evidence extraction for the comparative study of map signs within cartographic culture and geohistorical research.

AI.brief_summary: 提出两阶段框架，用于历史地图中地图符号的检测与可解释符号嵌入生成，并发布跨符号类别与绘图风格的开放基准 CaSiDD，方法上用 YOLOv10-X 做检测、以改造的 RADIOv4 骨干生成兼顾形式与语义的嵌入。
